raw_signal: (no owner signal -- this came out of a macro pass, not out of a sentence)
observations: At 390x844 and 320x844, at the scroll position the application sets itself, 0 of the board's 370px (300px at 320) is in the viewport during the tension, claim and confidence steps: 12 of 12 stage samples at each width across three decisions.
At 1440x900 the identical script runs the same steps with 99-100% of the board visible, scrollY 0 throughout.

The mechanism is `client/src/components/CommitmentScreen.tsx`: on the arrival of a move, if the panel's top is below 0.7 * innerHeight the panel is scrolled with `block: "start"`. Measured as an app-driven smooth scroll 0 -> 74 -> 297 -> 580 -> 764 -> 802, sampled at 100ms with every activation performed as an in-page `el.click()` so the harness never scrolls.
`block: "end"` was built and walked: scrollY 790 instead of 802 and the board still 0%, because `.commitment-screen` is 833px on an 844px viewport and aligning THE PANEL any way fills the screen.

THE SIZE-CONSTRAINT EXPLANATION IS FALSIFIED. Sweeping the whole scroll range with the move placed: board at document y=273 height 370, open step at y=1012 height 342, viewport 844. 133 scroll positions have the open step FULLY visible and some board visible; the best, y=510, shows 133 of 370px -- 36%, three ranks -- with the entire question on screen. The app scrolls to 802.

`docs/INTERACTION_GEOMETRY.md` states DECIDE's centre is coupled and that the layout serving it is two adjacent regions, explicitly not a single column with the board on top. The phone is one column with the board on top.
The record carries no viewport class. If co-visibility is a condition, decisions taken under the two conditions are pooled today with nothing distinguishing them.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Co-visibility is not part of the measurement; the declaration is made from an orientation already formed
candidate_mechanisms.explains: The scroll, which `CommitmentScreen`'s docblock argues for on the ground that the board has to be visible WHILE THE MOVE IS CHOSEN and that what is wrong is being left below the fold afterwards.
candidate_mechanisms.does_not_explain: Why the desktop then shows the board at 99-100% during the same steps, which on this reading is the odd one out rather than the correct case.
candidate_mechanisms.discriminator: OWNER. Nothing in the repository answers it.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Co-visibility is part of the measurement, and the phone layout loses it
candidate_mechanisms.explains: `INTERACTION_GEOMETRY.md`'s coupled centre, and the desktop's behaviour.
candidate_mechanisms.discriminator: OWNER, and then FIELD for whether a reading declared with the position off screen differs from one declared with it on screen.

candidate_mechanisms.name: The phone has no room and the 0% is arithmetic
candidate_mechanisms.explains: That both `block: "start"` and `block: "end"` leave it at 0%.
candidate_mechanisms.does_not_explain: The 133 scroll positions that have both. The panel is 833px of an 844px viewport, but the OPEN STEP is 342px and the board's lower half is 185px.

design_distinction: Scrolling a panel into view and scrolling a QUESTION into view are different intents, and on a viewport shorter than the panel they have different answers. The 0% is a consequence of the target, not of the height.
authority: OWNER for whether co-visibility is part of the measurement. REPO for the geometry and the scroll that produces it, both settled. FIELD for any effect on what is declared.
must_not_change: Nothing yet. An alignment change, a scroll-margin or a layout change would alter the conditions under which a declaration is collected, and whether that is a repair or a contamination depends on the answer to the owner question.
perceptual_success_criterion: UNDEFINED UNTIL THE OWNER ANSWERS. If co-visibility is a condition, it is that the question and some of the position share a screen on every viewport. If it is not, it is that they do not, on every viewport, and the desktop changes instead.
check: `docs/neta/harness/` -- `e4-board-covisibility.mjs` for the 0%, and the scroll-range sweep for the 133 positions.
next_step: One sentence from the owner: is the position required to be on screen while the reading is declared? A yes makes the phone layout a defect and probably makes viewport class a recorded condition. A no makes the desktop the odd one out and makes this closed. Until then nothing here is built, and no field is added to the record -- adding one before the answer would be encodability bias, which is exactly what `FL-005` is about.
